resources.string:
Copy the extracted DATA directory of your own PAL RMCP01 Mario Kart Wii disc to:

%1$s

For example with adb: adb push DATA /sdcard/Android/data/org.wiicompiled.quest/files/WiiCompiledOpenXRVR/DATA

Then start the app again.
The game is still running in the background.
The game opens in the headset.

The game is ready, but its game files (DATA) are missing. Select your own PAL (RMCP01) disc image to extract them, or import a game file from your computer that includes them.

The game files go to:
%1$s

Nothing from Mario Kart Wii comes with this app: each game is built from your own PAL (RMCP01) disc.

On this headset: copy your disc image (ISO, WBFS, RVZ…) here, for example into Download, press Select disc image, then Build on this Quest.

With a computer: in the WiiCompiled VR launcher, use Build for Quest with your disc image, copy the .wcgame file it makes to this headset, then press Import from computer. Retro Rewind also needs its pack, which this app can download from Retro Rewind's own server, or a Retro Rewind game file can carry.

The game files are ready. Now build this game from them: Build on this Quest takes about 30–40 minutes on a Quest 3. With a computer, use Build for Quest in the WiiCompiled VR launcher instead, copy the .wcgame file to this headset and press Import from computer.
This app was updated, so the game must be built again for it: press Build on this Quest, or use Build for Quest in the WiiCompiled VR launcher again and Import from computer.
Retro Rewind needs its pack (the RetroRewind6 folder) on this headset. It can be downloaded here from Retro Rewind\'s own server, or arrive with a Retro Rewind game file built with the pack included.

Retro Rewind\'s tracks, characters and code come from Retro Rewind\'s own distribution server, the same one the computer launcher uses. That is about 2 GB over Wi‑Fi.\n\nNothing from Retro Rewind comes with this app.
Retro Rewind publishes updates the same way it publishes the pack. Only what changed since version %1$s is downloaded.
Downloading the Retro Rewind pack from its own server. It carries on if you close this panel.
The Retro Rewind pack is ready.
The Retro Rewind pack could not be downloaded.\n%1$s
Gets the pack, and later its updates, from Retro Rewind\'s own server.
Build the game on this Quest?

The game is built on this headset from your own disc files. It takes about 30–40 minutes on a Quest 3 and uses most of its memory, so close other apps and keep the headset on its charger.\n\nThe first build downloads about 10 MB of Android build files from Google.
The installed game stays until the new build has finished.\n\nBuilding takes about 30–40 minutes on a Quest 3 and uses most of its memory, so close other apps and keep the headset on its charger.
Building the game from your disc files: about 30–40 minutes on a Quest 3. Keep the headset on its charger. The build carries on if you close this panel.
Build cancelled. Building again picks up where it stopped.
The game could not be built.\n%1$s
Downloading Android build files (%1$d of %2$d MB)
Checking the game file was built from your disc for this version of the app.
The game installed now stays until the new game file has been checked and completely imported.
DATA is there but incomplete or unreadable. Select your disc image to extract it again, or copy the whole extracted partition (sys/ and files/, not just files/) to:\n%1$s
The Retro Rewind pack is missing, so the game cannot start. Copy the RetroRewind6 folder (the one with Binaries, Tracks and Assets in it) to:\n%1$s
Reading the disc image and checking it is the clean PAL game.
The game files could not be set up.\n%1$s
This headset has no file picker to choose a disc image with.
Your current DATA folder stays until the new disc image has been checked and completely extracted.
The game could not be started.
Quest 1 cannot switch this settings panel into VR. Close it, then launch WiiCompiled VR from your library.
Removes what you tick below so it can be set up again from scratch. Your saves and settings stay.
Game files (DATA), with any unfinished extraction or import
Built games and the build workspace
Removing the files you chose. The launcher stays usable meanwhile.
The installation was reset. Select your disc image to set the game up again.
Reset cancelled. What was already removed stays removed.
The installation could not be reset completely.\n%1$s
Removes the game files, and if you tick them the built games and the Retro Rewind pack, so they can be set up again. Saves and settings stay.
The game folder could not be prepared: %1$s
Mods can alter how the game works. Start importing your first mod by clicking the button below.\n\nAs on the computer, mods change Retro Rewind. Import the mod\'s files, or the .zip it came in.
Each time Retro Rewind starts, the enabled mods are copied into its Patches folder. When two mods replace the same file, the one higher in the list wins.
The mod could not be imported
The mod could not be changed: %1$s
Are you sure you want to delete %1$s?
Deleting is permanent and cannot be undone.
This headset has no file picker to choose mod files with.
You are about to launch the game without mods. Do you want to clear your Patches folder? If you keep it, the game starts with the patches it holds still active.
The mods could not be installed
Mario Kart Wii recompiled to native code, with an OpenXR renderer, running on this headset. No game code and no game data come with it: each game is built from the disc you own.
Meta Quest port and the OpenXR VR renderer by iChris4.
The cockpit\'s turning steering wheel and hand steering by heurazy, from mario-kart-wii-VR-port (GPL v3).
WiiCompiled, the static recompilation this is built on, by patchzyy and the static recompilation community.
Retro Rewind by ZPL and team, the mod distribution this app can download and play.
Wheel Wizard by Patchzy and WantToBeeMe, the PC launcher this panel is modelled on.
aurora by encounter (MIT) with Google\'s Dawn: the graphics layer every frame goes through.
The OpenXR SDK by Khronos, and SDL 3 for windowing, audio and controllers.
nod by encounter, which reads your disc image, built into this app as libnod_jni.
On-headset builds use Termux\'s Android clang and lld, Google\'s Android NDK headers and libraries, and .NET for the translator.
The Dolphin emulator, the reference for how the Wii behaves.
GNU General Public License v3. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or associated with Nintendo. Mario Kart Wii is a trademark of Nintendo.
Changes apply the next time the game starts. While playing, press left Y to open the in-headset settings (click both thumbsticks together with Gamepad controllers).
The game is running, so these changes wait until it is closed and started again.
Plays races on the same flat screen as the menus instead of all around you. The camera settings below do not apply while it is on.
Ride behind the kart like the game, or sit in the driver\'s seat.
In first person, follow turning only (the comfortable choice), turning and climbing, or all kart rotation including banking.
Your driver sits where your eyes are. Other racers are never hidden.
The cockpit puts you at the driver\'s eyes, life-size, with the steering wheel or handlebar turning within reach. Custom uses the head offsets from the in-headset settings.
In the cockpit, squeeze a grip near the steering wheel or handlebar to grab it, and turn it to steer. Releasing both grips gives steering back to the stick. Hand steering by heurazy.
Tilts the race view back for playing reclined. 0 applies no tilt.
Scales the eye resolution the headset recommends. Higher is sharper and costs GPU time; lower it if races stutter.
How hard the headset clocks its CPU and GPU for the game. Boost gives the most speed; lower it if the headset gets hot or the battery matters more.
Experimental. Renders extra frames between game frames at the headset\'s rate. Needs GPU headroom and adds one game frame of latency.
Race HUD on the virtual screen
Puts the minimap, position and item roulette on a screen in front of you instead of stretching them across the view.
How far the menu screen and race HUD sit in front of you.
How wide the menu screen and race HUD are.
Shows your room through the headset\'s cameras around the menus instead of black. Races stay fully virtual, except in Flat Screen mode.
The game\'s own render size. Native keeps the headset at its best frame rate.
Bloom\'s bright glow reads poorly in a headset, so it starts off.
Skips a draw for a moment while its shader compiles instead of pausing the game.
Prepares the drawing on a second CPU core so busy scenes keep their speed. Turn off only to compare against the single-threaded path. Takes effect on the next launch.
What the Touch controllers are to the game.
The game\'s rumble vibrates the controllers.
Aim and move the right controller
Silences the game without changing the volumes above.
Replaces DATA with the files of your own PAL disc image.
Your disc image must be the clean PAL game: as a .iso file its MD5 hash is %1$s. Compressed images (WBFS, RVZ…) have a different hash.
Built for another version of this app; build it again
Builds the game from DATA on this headset: about 30–40 minutes on a Quest 3.
Installs a .wcgame made by Build for Quest in the WiiCompiled VR launcher on a computer.
Writes VR frame timing to the run log once per second: late, skipped and black frames, tracking loss. Turn it on to report stutter, and off again afterwards.
The game is not installed. Open WiiCompiled VR and set it up from Home.
